claims.text: As-received Q235 steel has inclusions and residual stresses arising from conventional processing.
Controlled stress-relief annealing can reduce residual stresses in Q235 steel.
Controlled surface finishing can minimize microstructural defects at the Q235 steel surface.
Temperature affects oxide-formation kinetics and passive-film stability in chloride-rich environments.
Lower surface-defect density promotes formation of a more homogeneous and adherent passive iron-oxide layer.
Lower residual stress promotes formation of a more homogeneous and adherent passive iron-oxide layer.
A homogeneous, adherent passive iron-oxide layer acts as a barrier to aggressive ions.
The greater defect content of untreated Q235 steel causes passive-film inconsistency and localized breakdown.
Passive-film inconsistency and localized breakdown accelerate corrosion.
Treated Q235 steel will have a lower corrosion rate than untreated Q235 steel under identical chloride-rich conditions.
Treated Q235 steel will develop fewer localized corrosion sites than untreated Q235 steel.
Treated Q235 steel will form a more uniform and protective oxide layer than untreated Q235 steel.
The corrosion-suppressing effect will occur at both room temperature and moderately elevated temperature.
Environmental extremes or changes in environmental chemical composition may introduce additional corrosion-governing variables.
